claims.statement: Tom Allen was announced to meet Sullivan for $2,500 a side in the twenty-four-foot ring, but the match did not come off.
Richard K. Fox wants to back Tom Allen against John L. Sullivan or any other pugilist for the championship of the world.
Tom Allen issued a challenge to fight John L. Sullivan, the American champion.
Richard K. Fox deposited $1,000 with Harry Hill to show that Tom Allen wanted to fight.
Richard K. Fox posted $1,000 with Harry Hill on 9 October 1882, offering to match Tom Allen against any man in America.
The proposed match was for $1,000 to $2,500 a side and the championship of the world, within 100 miles of New Orleans, to take place within three months of signing articles.
Richard K. Fox deposited money with Harry Hill (amount printed as '$1,') as part of a challenge on Tom Allen's behalf.

Richard K. Fox issued a challenge on Tom Allen's behalf to fight any pugilist, John L. Sullivan preferred, for the championship, at $1,000 to $2,500 a side, within three months of signing articles, near New Orleans.
Richard K. Fox deposited money with Harry Hill (amount printed as '$1,') as part of a challenge on Tom Allen's behalf.

Richard K. Fox issued a challenge offering to back Tom Allen, the ex-champion of America, to fight any pugilist, John L. Sullivan preferred, for the championship of the world, within three months of signing articles.
Richard K. Fox deposited $1,000 with Harry Hill and issued a challenge on behalf of Tom Allen.
Fox offered to back Tom Allen to fight any pugilist, John L. Sullivan preferred, for the championship of the world.
Sullivan was notified to accept the challenge issued on Tom Allen's behalf, to fight within three months and within one hundred miles of Kansas City.
Tom Allen offered to fight Jno. L. Sullivan for a stake printed as $1,000 to $5,000.
A sum was posted with Harry Hill and John L. Sullivan was defied to cover it; the fragment does not name the depositor.
Richard Fox proposed to wager $5,000 that Tom Allen could defeat John L. Sullivan in the prize ring.
Richard Fox posted $1,000 with Harry Hill to cover his challenge to John L. Sullivan.
Mr. Harding, Allen's representative, did not go to Harry Hill's theatre to settle the $1,000 match.
Farrell, a friend of Sullivan, claimed the $1,000 that Fox had posted.
A proposed prize fight for $2,500 a side between Tom Allen and John L. Sullivan was under discussion in Boston sporting circles.
Sullivan sent word to Richard K. Fox that he would fight Tom Allen for $5,000 a side, or for any sum Fox could raise, in Colorado or the Indian Territory.
Fox would match Jim Mace against Sullivan only if Sullivan defeated Tom Allen.
Tom Allen challenged John L. Sullivan or any man in the world to fight for $1,600 or $5,000 a side and the championship of the world, under London prize ring rules.
Allen's backer posted $1,000 to back the challenge.
Allen was to meet the champion's representative in New York on November 10, 1882 to arrange the match.
Sullivan's backer named November 10 to meet and sign articles for the match with Allen.
Allen offered to meet Sullivan or any pugilist at the Police Gazette office on November 16 to arrange a match.
Sullivan told Harry Hill he would be in New York on November 20 to sign articles to fight Tom Allen.
After Allen's exhibition, the chance of a fight between Tom Allen and John L. Sullivan was considered scarcely probable.
John L. Sullivan said at the exhibition that he had not come to make a match with Tom Allen and would not be permitted to spar with him.
In Chicago Tom Allen refused to take part in a fixed fight with Jim Elliott, proposed by 'the Parson' and others.
Tom Allen said he would make no match until after the Sullivan and Elliott fight, and would then fight the winner with bare knuckles or gloves.
Richard K. Fox telegraphed Charles Davies in Chicago that he would not back Tom Allen against Elliott and had dropped Allen altogether, because of Allen's conduct since leaving New York.
Tom Allen said he would fight the winner of the Sullivan-Elliott glove contest if he recovered.

After a consultation with R. K. Fox in New York, Tom Allen agreed to accept James Elliott's challenge to fight him for $1,000 and the championship of America, within six weeks of signing articles and within 1,000 miles of New Orleans.
Tom Allen did not appear at Charles E. Davies' place in Chicago on December 14, 1882, to sign articles for a prize fight with Jimmy Elliott.
A match between Tom Allen and Jim Elliott was to be arranged on Friday, December 15, 1882, in Chicago.
George Morrow offered to bet $500 that Tom Allen could not knock out J. Miles in four three-minute rounds.
Mitchell issued a challenge to meet Slade, Sullivan, Jem Mace, Joe Goss or Tom Allen for $5,000 to $10,000 a side; the men named did not reply.
Tom Allen offered an unnamed man to meet Duncan C. Ross in a mounted or on-foot broadsword contest for $500 a side or a $1,000 stake.
Tom Allen deposited $200 with the Post-Dispatch as a forfeit to guarantee a sword match with Duncan C. Ross.
Duncan C. Ross was in the city on Thursday and Friday, saw Tom Allen's challenge, and paid no attention to it.
Tom Allen withdrew his $200 forfeit, placed with the Post-Dispatch for a sword match between Duncan C. Ross and August Schmitt, because Ross had not covered it.
Tom Allen deposited $160 for Flint on Saturday, and the McManus party covered it.
Tom Allen, who had the power to act for Flint, took part in arranging a fight to a finish between Flint and McManus at 160 pounds, with skin gloves under Queensberry rules.
Tom Allen witnessed the signing of the articles for the Flint and McManus fight.
Jack King says he has $50 in Tom Allen's hands for a fight between Allen and Mike Boden, and asks Allen to cover it and arrange a match.
According to Jack King, Tom Allen has been talking about fighting anybody in St. Louis.
Tom Allen said he told Dutch Niel he would give $50 towards a purse for a contest between Niel and Johnnie Daly.
Tom Allen denied that he would furnish a $500 side bet for Dutch Niel, and said he was not prepared to wager $500 on the result.
Dutch Niel said he had been given to understand that Tom Allen would furnish a stake for him in a contest with Johnnie Daly.
Tom Allen wrote to Ed Smith several weeks before December 1893 advising him to try to arrange a match with Jackson.
Ed Smith wrote to Tom Allen, in a letter received on 22 December 1893, that his next fight would be with the winner of the Corbett-Mitchell fight.
Tom Allen announced he would back Al J. Neist against Mike Mooney in a lightweight wrestling match, any style, for $250 a side, winner take all.
Jem Mace wanted to come to America and fight Tom Allen again, after hearing that Allen had said he could whip him.
Tom Allen said he would back Denver Ed Smith if Smith could get a match with a prominent pugilist, and Smith would then probably train in St. Louis.
Tom Allen said he would back Denver Ed Smith if Smith could get a fight with any of the big heavyweights.
